title: Nursing and Billing Bulletin: Care Level Changes During an Assisted Living Respite Stay
content:
Under the Respite and Short-Term Stay Agreement the assisted living respite care levels — Assisted Living Respite Stay (Standard Care), (Enhanced Care) and (Extensive Care) — are set by the care-point band of the most recent nurse assessment.

## Rules in force

1. **Which level applies.** The care level of an assisted living respite guest is the one whose care-point band contains the score of the most recent nurse assessment.
2. **Between which stay types, and when.** A level change is possible only between the three assisted living respite stay types and only while the stay is in stay. The stay status read is the one on the stay record.
3. **Needs beyond the stay.** A score above the highest care-point score accepted by the Assisted Living Respite Stay (Extensive Care), 75 points, or a new wander risk, means the guest's needs exceed the stay and the stay ends with the family arranging other care.
4. **Trial stays.** An Independent Living Trial Stay guest found to need care does not change stay type mid-stay.

## Retired provision

The former provision is no longer in force that, where an assessment during the stay places the guest in another assisted living respite level, the stay type changes from the assessment date, the remaining nights of the current segment are credited as a level-change adjustment credit referencing that segment, and the same nights are charged as a level-change segment at the new level's nightly rate published on the booking date. Each of these three parts is superseded by the current basis.

## Points of judgement

| Situation on the stay record | Level change possible |
|---|---|
| Assisted Living Respite Stay (Standard Care), in stay, new assessment in the Enhanced Care band | Yes — between assisted living respite stay types, while in stay |
| Assisted Living Respite Stay (Enhanced Care), booked, not yet checked in | No — the stay is not in stay |
| Assisted Living Respite Stay (Extensive Care), in stay, new assessment of 80 points | No — the score is above 75; the guest's needs exceed the stay and the stay ends with the family arranging other care |
| Assisted Living Respite Stay (Standard Care), in stay, a new wander risk | No — the guest's needs exceed the stay and the stay ends with the family arranging other care |
| Independent Living Trial Stay, in stay, guest found to need care | No — a trial stay does not change stay type mid-stay |
| Memory Care Respite Stay or Post-Hospital Recovery Stay | No — neither is one of the three assisted living respite stay types |

superseded_clauses: Where an assessment during the stay places the guest in another assisted living respite level, the stay type changes from the assessment date
the remaining nights of the current segment are credited as a level_change_adjustment credit referencing that segment
the same nights are charged as a level_change segment at the new level's nightly_rate published on the booking date
